sections.html:
Most slowdowns come from people outside your control, such as a lender waiting on approval, an appraiser with a full calendar, or a repair list that keeps growing after the inspection. A direct cash sale avoids most of them, though a fairly priced listing can still sell briskly in Franklin County.

Whatever path you pick, pin down three facts first: the payoff on any mortgage, the year's tax status, and the school district and municipality for the parcel. The city spills across so many districts and suburban borders that buyers ask about all three right away.

No Ohio city covers more ground than Columbus, a result of annexing suburbs that needed city water lines. The city measures about 223 square miles, with 4,116 people per square mile at the 2020 census. Growth has continued: 938,396 residents in mid-2025, a 3.6% gain on the 906,215 base of April 2020 and far above the 787,033 counted in 2010.

Annexation crossed many school and township lines, so a Columbus address may fall in Columbus City Schools or in South-Western, Dublin, Hilliard, New Albany-Plain, Westerville or Worthington. Put the correct district on your listing sheet. Columbus City Schools alone runs 142 elementary, middle and high schools, and the suburban districts typically serve one or more townships, sometimes crossing municipal lines. A buyer with children will check the boundary against the district's own map, so give the street address exactly as the county records it.

Best known are the Arena District, Brewery District, Clintonville, Franklinton, German Village, the Short North and Victorian Village, each with its own mix of houses and buyers. Victorian Village is known for its Victorian houses facing Goodale Park.

  • Core neighborhoods: confirm the exact name buyers use for your block, since listings are searched by neighborhood.
  • Outer areas: confirm the school district and whether the parcel is inside Columbus or a neighboring suburb.
  • Riverside and creek-side parcels: the region has a history of flooding, including the Great Flood of 1913, so ask the city or county about flood-zone status before you list a low-lying house.

On the 2020-2024 survey, the median owner-occupied Columbus home is worth $252,900. Owners occupy 44.1% of homes across 390,528 households that average 2.28 people. Rent typically runs $1,295 a month, and the middle household earns $66,082.

As the state capital, Columbus gets most of its jobs from government, and Ohio State University with its Wexner Medical Center keeps demand steady near campus and downtown.

The conveyance fee is $3 per $1,000, made up of $1 for the state and $2 for the county commissioners.

Franklin County Auditor transfer tax and conveyance fee schedule
ChargeAmount
Conveyance fee$3 per $1,000 of the sale price
Conveyance fee when the grantor receives the homestead exemption$1 per $1,000, because the county's permissive part is waived
Minimum conveyance fee$3
Transfer tax$0.50 on every non-exempt transfer
Exempt transfersOnly the $0.50 transfer tax
Accepted paymentCash, business check or cashier's check payable to the Franklin County Auditor

Personal checks are refused, and the sale amount is rounded up to the next $100. The department moves more than 30,000 transfers each year, and its number is 614-525-3253. Ohio Revised Code 319.202 and 319.54(G)(3) define which transfers are exempt.

Street numbering radiates from Broad and High Streets downtown, climbing at about 700 numbers to the mile. Interstate 70 runs east and west, Interstate 71 runs north and southwest, and the two share about a mile and a half downtown at the spot locals call The Split, a known rush-hour choke point. Workers average 21.5 minutes to get to a job.

Mention how close the house is to an interstate ramp, and to the Split, because both shape the commute a buyer pictures.

sections.h2: Property tax and the homestead exemption
sections.html:
Property tax in Franklin County is paid in two installments, and a bill that never arrived is no excuse for paying late. Owners with no bill in hand should call 614-525-3438. At closing, the settlement statement divides the tax between buyer and seller, and your escrow officer can walk through that entry.

The standard homestead exemption is a credit aimed at older or disabled owners: age 65 by the end of the year being applied for, or total and permanent disability on January 1, plus primary residence and a qualifying income. A richer version with no income test goes to owners rated 100% disabled from military service, and it removes the tax on $50,000 of appraised value. Because a seller who holds the exemption cuts the conveyance fee to $1 per $1,000, check the Auditor's property search for the Homestead Credit status before closing.

  • Auditor's property search: lists the Homestead Credit status of your parcel.
  • Treasurer: confirms the status of the year's tax and any bill you did not receive.
  • Closing statement: shows the buyer-seller tax split before you sign.

sections.h2: Short-term rentals and the disclosure form
sections.html:
For nightly rentals, the short-term rental permit comes from the License Section of Building and Zoning Services at 4252 Groves Road, phone 614-645-8366. A house that was ever advertised on a booking platform invites buyer questions about that permit.

Revised Code 5302.30 sets the disclosure form for residences of up to four units, excusing court-ordered sales, estate fiduciaries and gifts to direct-line relatives. Severe thunderstorms and the occasional tornado can hit in spring, so known roof or hail damage belongs on the disclosure form.

After you accept an offer, an escrow officer opens the file, orders the title search and prepares the deed. Pull together your latest tax bill, mortgage payoff details, and permits or receipts for past work. If the property was a short-term rental or has a tenant, bring those records too.

On closing day you sign the deed in front of a notary, the buyer's money comes in, and the escrow officer clears your loan, splits the year's tax and wires you what is left. The deed then goes to the Franklin County Auditor for the conveyance fee and transfer stamp before the recorder files it. With cash there is usually no lender appraisal, so one frequent cause of delay disappears.

Rank offers by what lands in your account after the conveyance fee, the tax split and any repair credit, and write the closing date into the contract.

faqs.q: How are conveyance fees figured in Franklin County?
faqs.a: At $3 for each $1,000 of price, with a $3 floor and a $0.50 transfer tax. A grantor who holds the homestead exemption at transfer pays $1 per $1,000 instead.

faqs.q: Does the Auditor take personal checks?
faqs.a: No. Cash, business checks and cashier's checks made out to the Franklin County Auditor are accepted, and the amount must be exact or the transfer will not process.

faqs.q: Could my Columbus house be in a suburban school district?
faqs.a: Yes, depending on the parcel. Columbus City Schools is the biggest system at 55,000 pupils, yet parts of the city belong to South-Western, Dublin, Hilliard, New Albany-Plain, Westerville or Worthington. Check your tax bill or ask the county.

faqs.q: My Columbus house used to be a short-term rental. Does that affect the sale?
faqs.a: The permit applies to operating the rental, and the License Section of Building and Zoning Services issues it. Ask that office at 614-645-8366 whether yours is current, since a buyer is likely to ask.

faqs.q: What if my Franklin County tax bill never arrived?
faqs.a: Call the treasurer at 614-525-3438. A bill that never showed up does not erase penalty and interest.
